## Purpose and Runtime
BeeCount is an offline-first personal-finance mobile app for Android and iOS: ledgers, accounts, transactions, budgets, analytics, imports/exports, automation, AI-assisted bookkeeping, and optional cloud synchronization. Flutter 3.27+ is the primary runtime; Riverpod manages application state and Drift/SQLite persists local data. Native Android and iOS hosts provide lifecycle, widgets, notifications, screenshots, and platform integrations.

Entry sequence: `lib/main.dart` starts Flutter, `lib/app.dart` constructs the application shell, and `lib/providers.dart` / `lib/providers/all_providers.dart` establish shared state and dependency wiring.

## Presentation and Feature Composition
Feature pages are organized by domain and consume Riverpod providers, repositories, and services rather than directly owning persistence. Main navigation surfaces include home, analytics, ledgers, and settings under `lib/pages/main/home_page.dart`, `lib/pages/main/analytics_page.dart`, and `lib/pages/main/ledgers_page_new.dart`. Transaction editing is centered on `lib/pages/transaction/transaction_editor_page.dart`; account, budget, category, tag, and report screens form related domain UI.

The presentation boundary is `lib/pages/` and `lib/widgets/`; mutable application state and derived queries live in `lib/providers/`.

## Local Financial Data Layer
The local database schema and generated Drift bindings are rooted in `lib/data/db.dart` and `lib/data/db.g.dart`. Repository interfaces isolate domain reads/writes; `lib/data/repositories/repositories.dart` groups them, while implementations such as `lib/data/repositories/local/local_transaction_repository.dart` and `lib/data/repositories/local/local_account_repository.dart` bind to SQLite.

Primary flow is UI/provider → repository → local database. Domain services coordinate cross-entity invariants such as transaction creation, transfers, category matching, recurring records, and exchange-rate calculations: `lib/services/billing/bill_creation_service.dart`, `lib/services/data/recurring_transaction_service.dart`, and `lib/services/currency/exchange_rate_service.dart`.

## Sync Architecture and External Storage
Cloud synchronization layers on top of local persistence rather than replacing it. `lib/cloud/sync/sync_coordinator.dart` and `lib/cloud/sync/sync_engine.dart` orchestrate changes, serialization, pull/apply, conflicts, attachments, profiles, and realtime events. `lib/cloud/sync/change_tracker.dart` records local mutation state, while `lib/cloud/sync/sync_conflict_resolver.dart` handles reconciliation.

Reusable provider contracts are in `packages/flutter_cloud_sync/lib/src/core/cloud_provider.dart`; adapters support BeeCount Cloud, iCloud, Supabase, WebDAV, and S3. Material external services include self-hosted BeeCount Cloud (auth/database/storage/realtime), Apple iCloud, Supabase, WebDAV servers, and S3-compatible storage. Provider-specific implementations include `packages/flutter_cloud_sync_supabase/lib/src/supabase_provider.dart`, `packages/flutter_cloud_sync_icloud/lib/src/icloud_provider.dart`, and `packages/flutter_cloud_sync_s3/lib/src/s3_provider.dart`.

## AI and Agent Pipeline
AI bookkeeping supports structured extraction from text, images/OCR, and voice, then routes results into the ordinary bill-creation path. Core extraction contracts and prompt/JSON handling reside in `lib/ai/core/ai_extraction_engine.dart`, `lib/ai/core/prompt_builder.dart`, and `lib/services/ai/ai_bookkeeper.dart`. Provider selection/configuration is isolated in `lib/ai/providers/ai_provider_factory.dart`.

The agent feature is a permissioned tool-execution boundary: conversation UI → app facade → agent core/model → authorized local tools and memory. App integration is in `lib/services/ai/agent_app_facade.dart`; authorization and persisted settings are in `lib/agent/permission/agent_authorization_gate.dart` and `lib/agent/runtime/agent_execution_settings.dart`. Shared protocol/core abstractions live in `packages/agentcore/lib/src/agent_core.dart` and `packages/agentcore/lib/src/protocol/openai_compatible_transport.dart`. OpenAI-compatible and Zhipu GLM providers are supplied by local packages.

## Import, Export, Automation, and Maintenance
Import translates source files into domain records through parsers before persistence: `lib/services/data_import_service.dart`, `lib/services/import/csv_parser.dart`, and provider-specific parsers such as `lib/services/import/parsers/alipay_parser.dart`. Export/config and attachment transfer are handled separately by `lib/services/export/config_export_service.dart` and `lib/services/attachment_export_import_service.dart`.

Recurring and automatic billing are scheduled domain operations in `lib/services/automation/auto_billing_service.dart`. Orphan scanning/cleanup protects local consistency in `lib/services/maintenance/orphan_scanner.dart` and `lib/services/maintenance/orphan_cleaner.dart`.

## Native Integration and Widgets
Flutter delegates OS-specific behaviors to Android Kotlin and iOS Swift. Android starts through `android/app/src/main/kotlin/com/tntlikely/beecount/MainActivity.kt`; iOS through `ios/Runner/AppDelegate.swift`. Screenshot monitoring and notification interactions have Android receivers/services, while iOS exposes app intents and auto-billing bridging.

Widget data is derived in Flutter by `lib/widget/widget_data_service.dart` and rendered/spec’d through `lib/widget/widget_manager.dart` and `lib/widget/widget_spec.dart`; native widget extensions/providers display it, including `android/app/src/main/kotlin/com/tntlikely/beecount/BeeCountWidgetProvider.kt` and `ios/BeeCountWidget/BeeCountWidgetBundle.swift`.
